test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Access to EMS software and data logs.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS software interface for a continuous period of at least 10 minutes.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are displayed in real-time for all monitored GMP storage areas.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS interface showing real-time temperature data.

test_steps.action: Access the system logs or data export feature to review recorded temperature data for the observed period.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less for each monitored area.
data_to_capture: Exported data log showing timestamps and temperature values.

acceptance_criteria: All GMP storage areas show continuous temperature monitoring.
Recorded temperature data confirms intervals do not exceed 5 minutes.
data_integrity_requirements: Data is recorded accurately and without loss.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range, Accuracy, and Alarm Deviation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates within the specified temperature range and accuracy, and generates alerts when temperature deviates from the setpoint.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Access to EMS software and alarm configuration.
Calibrated reference thermometer.

test_steps.action: Set a target temperature within the specified range (e.g., 20°C) and configure a setpoint with a ±2°C deviation alarm.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS accepts the setpoint and alarm deviation configuration.

test_steps.action: Using a calibrated reference thermometer, introduce a temperature that is 1°C above the setpoint (e.g., 21°C) in a monitored area.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the temperature within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer, and no alarm is triggered.

test_steps.action: Introduce a temperature that is 2°C above the setpoint (e.g., 22°C) in the same monitored area.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the temperature within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer, and an alarm is triggered.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS displaying temperature and active alarm.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the normal operating range and verify the alarm clears.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm condition is cleared in the EMS.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of EMS showing alarm cleared.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-4 for a temperature below the setpoint (e.g., 18°C and 17°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the temperature within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer, and an alarm is triggered at 2°C deviation below setpoint.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of EMS displaying temperature and active alarm.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS accurately measures temperature within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer.
Alarms are generated when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
Alarms are cleared when temperature returns to the normal range.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events are logged correctly with timestamps.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Unmodified and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system uses vendor-supplied software without modification and that all data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Access to system logs and configuration files.
Access to the EMS database.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS system's software installation directory and compare file hashes or versions with the vendor's provided manifest.
test_steps.expected_result: All installed software files match the vendor's provided manifest, indicating no unauthorized modifications.

test_steps.action: Generate a sample temperature data report from the EMS system and examine the underlying data storage mechanism.
test_steps.expected_result: The data is stored in a format consistent with the vendor's standard database format (e.g., SQL tables, specific file structures).
data_to_capture: Description of the database structure and format.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system's software is confirmed to be unmodified from the vendor's supplied version.
The data storage format is verified to be the vendor's standard database format.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-003: The system shall use vendor-supplied software without modification.
URS-EMS-006: All data shall be stored in the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored in a format that ensures its integrity and can be reliably retrieved.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Alarm Notification Integration and Response Time
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system generates alerts when temperature deviates from setpoint and that these notifications integrate with the site paging system within the specified response time.
prerequisites: EMS system is operational and configured with setpoints.
Site paging system is operational and configured.
Access to EMS system logs and paging system logs.
Ability to simulate temperature deviations.

test_steps.action: Configure a temperature setpoint in the EMS system and simulate a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm (e.g., +2°C from setpoint).
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system generates an alarm notification.

test_steps.action: Observe the site paging system for the incoming alarm notification.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is received on the site paging system.
data_to_capture: Time of alarm notification on paging system.

test_steps.action: Record the time elapsed between the alarm trigger in the EMS system and the receipt of the notification on the paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: The elapsed time is less than or equal to 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: Total response time (alarm trigger to paging notification).

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification content on the paging system is clear and provides relevant information (e.g., location, temperature).
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm notification content is informative and actionable.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system successfully generates an alarm for temperature deviations.
Alarm notifications are successfully integrated with the site paging system.
The system response time for alarm conditions does not exceed 30 seconds.
Alarm notifications are clear and informative.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-005: The system shall generate alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint.
URS-EMS-015: Alarm notifications shall integrate with site paging system using vendor API.
URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events must be accurately logged and notifications must be reliably transmitted.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system maintains a comprehensive audit trail and supports electronic signatures as per 21 CFR Part 11.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
A simulated event requiring an audit trail entry (e.g., configuration change) is planned.

test_steps.action: Perform a configuration change within the EMS system (e.g., adjust a setpoint or alarm threshold).
test_steps.expected_result: The system logs the change in the audit trail, including user, date, time, and the nature of the change.
data_to_capture: Audit trail log entry for the configuration change.

test_steps.action: Initiate an action that requires an electronic signature (e.g., approving a report or acknowledging an alarm).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for and captures a valid electronic signature, including user ID, date, time, and reason for signature.
data_to_capture: Electronic signature record associated with the action.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail and electronic signature records for completeness and accuracy.
test_steps.expected_result: All recorded events and signatures are complete, accurate, and comply with 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
data_to_capture: Screenshots or exported reports of audit trail and electronic signature records.

acceptance_criteria: All configuration changes are logged in the audit trail with sufficient detail.
Electronic signatures are captured correctly for all required actions.
Audit trail and electronic signature data is unalterable and readily retrievable.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must be comprehensive, time-stamped, and secure.
Electronic signatures must be legally equivalent to handwritten signatures.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Archival and Storage Capacity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can store data for at least 10 years and that the archival feature functions correctly.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists or can be simulated to test archival.
Access to the vendor's standard database and archival mechanism is available.

test_steps.action: Verify the current data storage capacity and estimate the time required to reach the 10-year storage limit based on current data generation rates.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's current storage capacity is documented, and the estimated time to reach 10 years of data is calculated.
data_to_capture: Estimated time to fill storage capacity.

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's standard archival process for data older than a specified period (e.g., 1 year).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully archives the specified historical data, removing it from active storage but retaining it in an accessible archival format.
data_to_capture: Location and format of archived data.

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve data from the archived location to confirm its integrity and accessibility.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data is successfully retrieved and is readable and accurate.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system's active storage capacity is sufficient to support 10 years of continuous monitoring after archival.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's design and configuration support the retention of 10 years of continuous monitoring data.
data_to_capture: System configuration details related to data retention.
Confirmation of storage capacity meeting 10-year requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The system's data storage capacity is confirmed to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
The archival process successfully moves historical data to a designated archival location.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be retained for the specified period.
Archived data must be secure, accessible, and uncorrupted.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Usage for Batch Release
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system utilizes vendor-provided standard reports for batch release purposes as required.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Access to EMS reporting module is available.
Sample data exists within the system for reporting.

test_steps.action: Access the reporting module of the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The reporting module is accessible and displays available report options.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the reporting module interface.

test_steps.action: Select and generate a standard report relevant to batch release (e.g., temperature log for a specific period).
test_steps.expected_result: A report is generated successfully using the vendor's standard template and format.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report to confirm it contains accurate data and is in the vendor's standard format.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects the monitored data and adheres to the vendor's standard reporting layout.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates standard reports.
Generated reports are in the vendor's specified format.
Reports contain accurate and relevant data for batch release.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
data_integrity_requirements: Report data must be accurate and complete.
Report format must be consistent with vendor specifications.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system meets the specified availability requirement of 99.5%, excluding periods of planned maintenance.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is operational.
Access to system logs or monitoring tools that track uptime and downtime is available.
A schedule of planned maintenance activities is available.

test_steps.action: Obtain system uptime and downtime records for a defined period (e.g., 30 days).
test_steps.expected_result: System logs or monitoring tools provide accurate records of system operational status.

test_steps.action: Identify and exclude any downtime periods that correspond to documented planned maintenance.
test_steps.expected_result: Planned maintenance periods are clearly identified and can be excluded from availability calculations.
data_to_capture: List of planned maintenance dates and durations.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage based on the remaining operational time and the total time in the defined period.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage is determined.

test_steps.action: Compare the calculated availability percentage against the URS requirement of 99.5%.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability meets or exceeds the 99.5% requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The system achieves a minimum availability of 99.5% when planned maintenance is excluded.
Documentation of uptime/downtime and planned maintenance is sufficient to support the calculation.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Uptime and downtime records must be accurate and complete.
Planned maintenance records must be accurate and verifiable.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System can successfully interface with the existing facility management system using standard protocols.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System is installed and configured.
Facility Management System is operational and accessible.
Network connectivity between EMS and FMS is established.
Details of the standard protocols to be used are documented.

test_steps.action: Configure the EMS to send temperature and humidity data to the Facility Management System using the specified standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS successfully establishes a connection and begins transmitting data to the FMS.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of successful connection in EMS logs.
Confirmation of data reception in FMS logs.

test_steps.action: Monitor the Facility Management System to confirm receipt of temperature and humidity data from the EMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The FMS displays accurate and timely temperature and humidity readings from the EMS.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of FMS displaying received EMS data.
Timestamp of data reception in FMS.

test_steps.action: Introduce a minor, controlled deviation in temperature within a monitored area and verify that this deviation is reflected in the FMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The FMS accurately reflects the introduced temperature deviation within the expected reporting interval.
data_to_capture: Record of the controlled temperature deviation.
FMS screenshot showing the reflected deviation.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS successfully transmits data to the FMS.
The FMS accurately displays the received temperature and humidity data.
Controlled temperature deviations are correctly reflected in the FMS.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-014: System shall interface with existing facility management system via standard protocols.
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted to FMS must be accurate and complete.
Data transmission must occur within defined intervals.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System meets the required availability of 99.5% and that planned maintenance periods are correctly excluded from availability calculations.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System has been operational for a sufficient period to gather availability data (e.g., 1 month).
A log of all system downtime, including planned maintenance, is available.
The definition of 'planned maintenance' is clearly documented.

test_steps.action: Review the system's operational logs and downtime records for a defined period (e.g., the last month).
test_steps.expected_result: All instances of system downtime are clearly identified and categorized as either planned maintenance or unplanned outage.
data_to_capture: System uptime/downtime log for the review period.

test_steps.action: Calculate the total operational time for the system during the review period.
test_steps.expected_result: The total operational time is accurately calculated based on the system's start and end times.

test_steps.action: Calculate the total unplanned downtime for the system during the review period.
test_steps.expected_result: The total unplanned downtime is accurately calculated by summing all downtime events not categorized as planned maintenance.

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage using the formula: ((Total Operational Time - Total Unplanned Downtime) / Total Operational Time) * 100.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage meets or exceeds the 99.5% requirement.

test_steps.action: Verify that all downtime events explicitly marked as 'planned maintenance' were excluded from the availability calculation.
test_steps.expected_result: Planned maintenance periods are demonstrably excluded from the availability calculation.
data_to_capture: Confirmation that planned maintenance downtime was not included in the calculation.

acceptance_criteria: The system availability is calculated to be 99.5% or higher.
Planned maintenance downtime is correctly excluded from the availability calculation.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate logging of all system uptime and downtime events is critical.
Clear distinction between planned and unplanned downtime is required.
